newsitem.title: CANADA: Internet cyberpals die in double suicide.
newsitem.headline: Internet cyberpals die in double suicide.

text.p: A relationship forged in cyberspace led to the double suicide of a transsexual from Chicago and a 21-year-old man from Orillia, Ontario, the first time they met in person, police said on Tuesday.

Sgt. Nigel Fontaine, a police spokesman, said the 24-year-old Chicago man and his Internet penpal checked into the Howard Johnson hotel in Toronto on Friday and were found dead two days later. Details began to come to light late on Monday.
A report from the Canadian Press news agency said the men were found in a bed with soft music playing. The agency said they died of an overdose using a drug recipe found on the Internet.
Reports in the media have said the man from Chicago was in the midst of a sex change. Fontaine said he could not confirm the names of the men or details the media have highlighted.

Fontaine said police interviews with family members revealed that the two men met over the Internet a few months ago but that this was the first time they had met face-to-face. Police said "writings" were found in the room although they would not confirm the existence of a suicide note.
"I think this is an absolute tragedy," Fontaine said. He said the police do not monitor the Internet for potential suicides but they do surf for evidence of hate crimes and pornography.
The Canadian Association for Suicide Prevention and the Samaritans both have Web sites to inform the public online about the dangers of suicide and offer help to the depressed.
